title: [v1.82.0-beta.1] Selfcontained version still asks for .NET 10
author: judaspriest
body_snippet:
Although @robertpopa22 mentioned in #8 that this is fixed in the next nighlty build, I still have the issue with version v1.82.0-beta.1

Tested with: 
v1.81.0 Latest Stable - Selfcontained x64 Windows
v1.82.0-beta.1 NB 3148 - Selfcontained x64 Windows


After the launch of mRemoteNG.exe I get the error message:

Missing Runtime: .NET 10.0
.NET 10.0.0 runtime library is required


Please download and install latest runtime:

https://..../runtime-desktop-10.0.3-windows-x64-installer


To properly ...

comments.author: judaspriest
comments.snippet:
UPDATE:

I can confirm, that this affects BOTH selfcontained versions: x86 + x64

20260303-v1.82.0-beta.1-NB-(3419)/mRemoteNG-20260303-v1.82.0-beta.1-NB-3418-x86-selfcontained.zip
20260303-v1.82.0-beta.1-NB-(3419)/mRemoteNG-20260303-v1.82.0-beta.1-NB-3418-x64-selfcontained.zip


Tested on:
Windows 11 Version 23H2 (Build 22631.6649), where .NET Desktop Runtime (8, 9, 10) was NEVER installed before and so the necessary registry key for mRemoteNG to launch (=hardcoded check for this registry path) ...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thanks for the detailed report and the registry key analysis @judaspriest!

**Root cause identified:** The self-contained build used a compile-time check (`#if !SELF_CONTAINED`) to skip the .NET registry check, but our CI builds with `Configuration=Release` which doesn't define `SELF_CONTAINED`. So the registry check ran even in self-contained builds.

**Fix applied:** Replaced the compile-time check with a **runtime detection** — the app now checks for `coreclr.dll` in the application directory...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Fixed in commit **[CENSORED!] Links to external GitHub repositories are not allowed** — the self-contained build now correctly bundles the .NET runtime without prompting for installation.
